title: Descent, exactness and detection for common-stage fibre functors
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $X$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and finite intermediate fields $E\subset L$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $B_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A_E/\varpi_E^n)_X$ and $E_X=B_{E,X}[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. These are the continuous completed coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete constructible integral categories with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], their bounded localized standard t-structures [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], and the pair category $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the finite scalar functors $T_{L/E}$ and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Write $\mathscr A_E(Z)$ for the finite-stage standard heart, $J_Z$ for its continuous rational realization [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], and $\omega_{\bar z,E}$ for the normalized exact finite-dimensional geometric fibre [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness]. Its lattice prescription on an affine etale chart of a lisse stratum is $M_{\bar z}=\varprojlim_n(N_n)_{\bar z}$ and $\omega_{\bar z,E}(F)=M_{\bar z}[1/\varpi_E]$, with a fractional lattice arrow $u/\varpi_E^a$ acting by $\varpi_E^{-a}\varprojlim_n u_n$.

Use the pair category [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], its common-stage calculus [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], and common standard heart [lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations]. Suppose the normalized finite-stage fibres are equipped with $\alpha,\beta$ satisfying the normalization and coherence of [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-pullback, lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-scalar]. There is an additive fibre functor $V_{\bar x}$ from the common heart to finite-dimensional $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-vector spaces, defined on heart pairs by $V_{\bar x}(E,F)=\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)\otimes_E\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. On an arrow $[M,u]:(E,F)\to(L,G)$ its map is $\omega_{\bar x,M}(u)\otimes_M\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, conjugated by the source and target $\beta$ identifications. This is independent of enlarging the coefficient field and replacing $u$ by $aT(u)a^{-1}$, preserves identities and composition, and extends to the isomorphism closure of the heart pairs with its natural comparison isomorphisms.

Every finite-stage heart inclusion preserves kernels and cokernels of heart arrows: these are the images of $H^{-1}C(u)$ and $H^0C(u)$ for a finite-stage cone, with their kernel and cokernel maps [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles, def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Images and homology of a finite heart complex are represented by the corresponding finite-stage objects. A finite-stage object whose image is zero in the common category becomes zero at some further coefficient stage; every short exact sequence in the common heart consequently admits a short exact finite-stage representative after one enlargement. Each $V_{\bar x}$ is exact. The family of these functors over all geometric points detects zero objects, isomorphisms, zero morphisms and short exact complexes, equivalently it is jointly conservative and gives the asserted map and exactness tests. Scalar extension $W\mapsto W\otimes_M\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ in these tests is faithful and exact; its map $w\mapsto w\otimes1$ is injective, and scalar extension identifies homology before and after extension [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact].

For the actual common-stage pullback [lem-per-adic-stratified-pullback-texact], the maps $\alpha_{g,F}\otimes_E\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ descend to natural pullback comparisons on $V$. They agree with the arrow prescription above under every common-stage representation, and satisfy identity and composite-pullback equations. The transition comparison is precisely $\beta$ extended to the algebraic closure with its balanced-tensor associator.

proof.text: Use [lem-per-common-stage-heart-exactness] to supply the exactness and finite representatives interface, then [lem-per-common-stage-fibre-transport] to obtain the normalized exact common fibre family with scalar and pullback coherence.

Apply [lem-per-common-stage-fibre-zero-map] to the family. Zero-object detection is zero-map detection applied to the identity. To reflect a monomorphism apply zero-map detection to its kernel inclusion; each fibre kills this inclusion by cancellation with the image monomorphism. Dually reflect epimorphisms using the cokernel projection. Thus fibrewise isomorphisms imply mono and epi and hence an isomorphism.

A short complex is exact iff its kernel inclusion composed with its cokernel projection is zero. Factor the mapped kernel inclusion through the target kernel and the mapped cokernel projection through the target cokernel. Fibrewise exactness makes their composite zero. Joint zero-map detection then gives exactness before taking fibres. Reflect mono and epi as above to reflect short exactness. The forward direction is the supplied CommonPoint exactness. Assemble these tests with the exactness and transport records.
